claims.text: MOA: macrolide that inhibits RNA synth by binding RNA polymerase; bactericidal vs C. diff.
claims.quote: Fidaxomicin is a macrolide antibacterial drug that inhibits RNA synthesis by binding to RNA polymerases. Fidaxomicin is bactericidal against C. difficile in vitro

claims.text: Treats: C. diff only (minimal to no gram (-) activity; minimal systemic absorption).
claims.quote: Fidaxomicin has minimal to no activity against gram-negative bacteria but is bactericidal against Clostridioides difficile (formerly Clostridium difficile). It is used exclusively for C. difficile infection because there is minimal systemic absorption.

claims.text: Know: abx of choice for an initial C. diff episode.
claims.quote: Fidaxomicin Clostridioides difficile (formerly Clostridium difficile) Antibiotic of choice for initial episode
DIFICID is contraindicated in patients who have known hypersensitivity to fidaxomicin or any other ingredient in DIFICID

claims.text: Allergy: some pts w fidaxomicin hypersensitivity also had other macrolide allergy; be aware in known macrolide allergy.
claims.quote: Some patients with hypersensitivity reactions to DIFICID also reported a history of allergy to other macrolides. Physicians prescribing DIFICID to patients with a known macrolide allergy should be aware of the possibility of hypersensitivity reactions.

claims.text: Pregnancy: minimal absorption, so fetal/infant risk should be relatively low.
claims.quote: Fidaxomicin has minimal systemic absorption, therefore risk of adverse effect to a fetus or breastfeeding infant should be relatively low.
claims.locator: Use of Macrolides During Pregnancy and Breastfeeding

claims.text: Caution: no jaundice or arrhythmias reported; little toxicity outside the GI tract.
claims.quote: Jaundice and arrhythmias are not reported with fidaxomicin. Because of minimal systemic absorption, there is very little chance of toxicity to any other organ system outside the GI tract.
